## Supplementary Figures

::: {#suppfig-pollen-coverage}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-02-pollen-coverage.png){width=90% fig-alt="Pollen-sequence coverage."}

**Pollen-sequence coverage.** This figure describes the `r format(preparation_pool_n, big.mark = ",")`-sequence preparation pool before analysis-specific predictor and control eligibility. Missing locations or intervals denote unavailable sequences, not absence of pollen-producing vegetation.
:::

::: {#suppfig-human-coverage}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-03-human-coverage.png){width=90% fig-alt="Human-proxy coverage."}

**Human-proxy coverage.** This figure shows SPD availability around the preparation pool under the 250 km neighbourhood with 500 km fallback. Missing coverage denotes insufficient dated evidence, not absence of people.
:::

::: {#suppfig-event-coverage}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-04-event-coverage.png){width=90% fig-alt="Regional pollen-event coverage."}

**Regional pollen-event coverage.** This figure distinguishes observed expert-screened chronologies from default-filled sequences in the preparation pool. An undetected or missing event does not imply human absence.
:::

::: {#suppfig-model-fit}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-22-hvarpart-profiles.png){width=90% fig-alt="HVarPart extraction-profile comparison."}

**HVarPart extraction-profile comparison.** This analysis compares signed, zero-truncated, and exclude-negative allocations for each analysis-specific available subset. Negative signed components retain suppressor/commonality meaning; missing decompositions are unavailable.
:::

::: {#suppfig-signed-results}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-25-h1-spatial-signed.png){width=90% fig-alt="Signed controlled spatial H1 contributions."}

**Signed controlled spatial H1 counterpart.** The controlled spatial H1 subset and time/space controls match @fig-h1-spatial. Negative values are signed human-minus-climate contribution differences, not negative explained variance; missing sequences are non-estimable.
:::

::: {#suppfig-dependence-controls}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-31-moran.png){width=90% fig-alt="Residual Moran diagnostic."}

**Residual Moran diagnostic.** This analysis tests spatial dependence before and after controls in the eligible spatial subset. Positive or negative Moran values indicate clustering direction; missing tests are non-estimable.
:::

::: {#suppfig-predictor-trajectories}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-16-predictor-spd.png){width=90% fig-alt="SPD temporal trajectories."}

**SPD temporal trajectories.** These trajectories show observed and HGAM-smoothed archaeological SPD within 8.5–2.0 ka BP continental-group and regional coverage. Missing segments indicate insufficient dates, not human absence; negative centred values are relative model-scale deviations.
:::

::: {#suppfig-spd-radius}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-35-spd-radius-spatial.png){width=90% fig-alt="Spatial SPD-radius comparison."}

**Spatial SPD-radius sensitivity.** This analysis compares strict 250 and 500 km predictors in `r format(radius_spatial_n, big.mark = ",")` matched sequences, with `r format(radius_spatial_defined_n, big.mark = ",")` defined zero-truncated pairs. Negative balances indicate greater climate allocation; missing pairs are not assigned zero.
:::

::: {#suppfig-event-sensitivity}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-38-event-spatial.png){width=90% fig-alt="Spatial event inclusion sensitivity."}

**Spatial human-event sensitivity.** This analysis compares SPD-only, event-only, and combined predictors in `r event_spatial_n` matched observed-event sequences. Negative balances indicate greater climate allocation; missing zero-truncated balances are retained as missing.
:::

::: {#suppfig-h2}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-01-h2-interrelationships.png){width=90% fig-alt="PAP ordination trajectories and zero-truncated human and climate allocations by continental group and region."}

**H2 PAP-interrelationship result.** Rows represent North America, Central and South America, Europe, Asia, and Oceania, and columns represent eligible regions defined from present-day Köppen–Geiger classes. Within each panel, grey circles show the distribution of pairwise Procrustes sum-of-squares distances among 500-year time slices, and the blue trajectory shows sample scores from the distance-based redundancy analysis from 8.5 ka BP (dark blue) towards 2.0 ka BP (light blue). Gold and teal arrows show the direction and relative strength of associations with human SPD and palaeoclimate, respectively. The adjacent bars show the zero-truncated human-climate composition for changes in relationships among all ten PAPs; negative signed contributions were set to zero before rescaling. Missing panels are non-estimable rather than evidence of stable PAP relationships or no driver effect. Signed contributions are shown in @suppfig-h2-signed.
:::

::: {#suppfig-record-examples}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-05-record-examples.png){width=90% fig-alt="Two updated pollen-sequence examples."}

**Updated sequence examples.** These trajectories show sequence-level PAP and predictor inputs for two illustrative sequences, without spatial aggregation. Negative signed HVarPart components retain suppressor/commonality meaning; missing values are unavailable, and examples are not representative subset summaries.
:::

::: {#suppfig-pap-n0}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-06-pap-n0.png){width=90% fig-alt="N0 PAP trajectory."}

**$N_0$ trajectory.** Equal-weighted posterior averages describe taxonomic richness over observed sequence coverage from 8.5 to 2.0 ka BP. Missing segments are unavailable; negative transformed predictions are model-scale quantities, not negative taxon counts.
:::

::: {#suppfig-pap-n1}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-07-pap-n1.png){width=90% fig-alt="N1 PAP trajectory."}

**$N_1$ trajectory.** Equal-weighted posterior averages describe Shannon-effective diversity over observed sequence coverage from 8.5 to 2.0 ka BP. Missing segments are unavailable; negative transformed predictions are model-scale quantities.
:::

::: {#suppfig-pap-n2}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-08-pap-n2.png){width=90% fig-alt="N2 PAP trajectory."}

**$N_2$ trajectory.** Equal-weighted posterior averages describe Simpson-effective diversity over observed sequence coverage from 8.5 to 2.0 ka BP. Missing segments are unavailable; negative transformed predictions are model-scale quantities.
:::

::: {#suppfig-pap-n1-minus-n2}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-09-pap-n1-minus-n2.png){width=90% fig-alt="N1 minus N2 PAP trajectory."}

**$N_1-N_2$ trajectory.** Equal-weighted posterior averages describe the separation of Shannon- and Simpson-effective diversity over observed coverage. Missing segments are unavailable, and signed transformed values retain their model-scale meaning.
:::

::: {#suppfig-pap-n2-n1}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-10-pap-n2-n1.png){width=90% fig-alt="N2 divided by N1 PAP trajectory."}

**$N_2/N_1$ trajectory.** Equal-weighted posterior averages describe dominance-sensitive evenness over observed 8.5–2.0 ka BP coverage. Missing segments are unavailable; negative transformed predictions are model-scale quantities.
:::

::: {#suppfig-pap-n1-n0}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-11-pap-n1-n0.png){width=90% fig-alt="N1 divided by N0 PAP trajectory."}

**$N_1/N_0$ trajectory.** Equal-weighted posterior averages describe richness-sensitive evenness over observed 8.5–2.0 ka BP coverage. Missing segments are unavailable; negative transformed predictions are model-scale quantities.
:::

::: {#suppfig-pap-roc}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-12-pap-roc.png){width=90% fig-alt="Rate-of-change PAP trajectory."}

**Rate-of-change trajectory.** Equal-weighted posterior averages describe pollen compositional change over observed sequence coverage. Missing segments are unavailable, and negative transformed predictions do not denote a negative ecological rate.
:::

::: {#suppfig-pap-dcca}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-13-pap-dcca.png){width=90% fig-alt="DCCA axis 1 PAP trajectory."}

**DCCA axis 1 trajectory.** Equal-weighted posterior averages describe the primary compositional gradient over observed sequence coverage. The axis sign is arbitrary; missing segments are unavailable rather than zero change.
:::

::: {#suppfig-pap-density-diversity}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-14-pap-density-diversity.png){width=90% fig-alt="Density-diversity PAP trajectory."}

**Density-diversity trajectory.** Equal-weighted posterior averages describe diversity change-point density over observed sequence coverage. Missing segments are unavailable, and negative transformed predictions are model-scale quantities.
:::

::: {#suppfig-pap-density-turnover}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-15-pap-density-turnover.png){width=90% fig-alt="Density-turnover PAP trajectory."}

**Density-turnover trajectory.** Equal-weighted posterior averages describe turnover change-point density over observed sequence coverage. Missing segments are unavailable, and negative transformed predictions are model-scale quantities.
:::

::: {#suppfig-temporal-signed}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-26-h1-temporal-signed.png){width=90% fig-alt="Signed controlled temporal H1 contributions."}

**Signed controlled temporal H1 counterpart.** The controlled temporal H1 subset and spatial dbMEM controls match @fig-h1-temporal. Negative contributions retain suppressor/commonality meaning; missing continental-group–age combinations are non-estimable.
:::

::: {#suppfig-pollen-retention}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-28-pollen-retention.png){width=85% fig-alt="Pollen-count threshold retention diagnostic."}

**Pollen retention and bias–coverage diagnostic.** The retention analysis compares rarefaction targets of 300, 500, and 1,000 grains, with associated sample minima of 50, about 83, and about 167 grains, against the 150-grain target and 25-grain sample-minimum baseline. It does not impose a 300- or 500-grain minimum on every sample and is not an H1 refit; missing strata have no retained sequences.
:::

::: {#suppfig-pap-collinearity}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-29-pap-collinearity.png){width=90% fig-alt="PAP correlation and HVarPart influence diagnostic."}

**PAP correlation and influence diagnostic.** The collinearity analysis uses paired sequences from the initial spatial analysis to evaluate response redundancy and contribution changes. Negative signed changes retain direction; missing pairs are excluded rather than assigned zero.
:::

::: {#suppfig-predictor-temp-annual}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-17-predictor-temp-annual.png){width=90% fig-alt="Annual temperature trajectories."}

**Annual-temperature trajectories.** These trajectories use point-extracted transient-climate values within the eligible pollen coverage. Missing segments are unavailable; negative centred values indicate relative model-scale deviations rather than invalid temperatures.
:::

::: {#suppfig-predictor-temp-cold}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-18-predictor-temp-cold.png){width=90% fig-alt="Coldest-month temperature trajectories."}

**Coldest-month temperature trajectories.** These trajectories use point-extracted transient-climate values within the eligible pollen coverage. Missing segments are unavailable; negative values retain their temperature or centred model-scale interpretation.
:::

::: {#suppfig-predictor-prec-summer}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-19-predictor-prec-summer.png){width=90% fig-alt="Summer precipitation trajectories."}

**Warm-season precipitation trajectories.** These trajectories use point-extracted transient-climate values within the eligible pollen coverage. Missing segments are unavailable; negative centred values are relative model-scale deviations.
:::

::: {#suppfig-predictor-prec-winter}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-20-predictor-prec-winter.png){width=90% fig-alt="Winter precipitation trajectories."}

**Cold-season precipitation trajectories.** These trajectories use point-extracted transient-climate values within the eligible pollen coverage. Missing segments are unavailable; negative centred values are relative model-scale deviations.
:::

::: {#suppfig-event-trajectories}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-21-event-trajectories.png){width=90% fig-alt="Regional pollen-event trajectories."}

**Regional pollen-event trajectories.** These trajectories show HGAM-smoothed expert-screened event evidence by continental group and region. Events are complementary and partly circular; missing segments are unavailable, and negative centred values are relative model-scale deviations.
:::

::: {#suppfig-pap-reduced}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-30-pap-reduced.png){width=90% fig-alt="Reduced-PAP response sensitivity."}

**Reduced-PAP response sensitivity.** The reduced-response analysis compares complete and reduced PAP responses within paired H1 sequences. Zero-truncated displays omit negative signed components; missing pairs are non-estimable.
:::

::: {#suppfig-adjusted-r2}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-23-adjusted-r2.png){width=90% fig-alt="Adjusted R-squared distribution."}

**Adjusted $R^2$ distributions.** This analysis reports total model fit for available spatial H1 decompositions by continental group and region. Negative adjusted $R^2$ values denote fits worse than the adjusted null benchmark; missing models are unavailable.
:::

::: {#suppfig-fit-importance}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-24-fit-importance.png){width=90% fig-alt="Model fit versus human importance."}

**Model fit versus human importance.** This analysis compares total adjusted $R^2$ with signed human hierarchical contribution in available spatial SPD models. Negative contributions retain suppressor/commonality meaning, and missing models are excluded rather than assigned zero.
:::

::: {#suppfig-h2-signed}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-27-h2-signed.png){width=90% fig-alt="Signed H2 contributions."}

**Signed H2 counterpart.** The H2 analysis subset and continental-group/region grouping match @suppfig-h2. Negative contributions retain suppressor/commonality meaning; missing panels are non-estimable.
:::

::: {#suppfig-thinning}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-32-thinning.png){width=90% fig-alt="Spatial thinning sensitivity."}

**Spatial thinning sensitivity.** The controlled SPD H1 profile is repeatedly thinned at 250 and 500 km. Negative balance values indicate greater climate allocation; missing replicate estimates are non-estimable.
:::

::: {#suppfig-leave-out}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-33-leave-out.png){width=90% fig-alt="Leave-one-group-out sensitivity."}

**Leave-one-group-out sensitivity.** The controlled SPD H1 profile omits each continental group or region in turn from its eligible subset. Negative balance values indicate greater climate allocation; missing exclusions lack an estimable comparison.
:::

::: {#suppfig-unique-fractions}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-34-unique-r2.png){width=90% fig-alt="Unique adjusted R-squared fractions."}

**Unique adjusted-$R^2$ fractions.** The controlled temporal comparison isolates non-shared human, climate, and spatial contributions in eligible continental-group–age sets. Fractions do not form a composition; negative values are valid adjusted estimates, and missing fractions are non-estimable.
:::

::: {#suppfig-radius-temporal}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-36-spd-radius-temporal.png){width=90% fig-alt="Temporal SPD-radius profiles."}

**Temporal SPD-radius profiles.** The spatially controlled analysis compares strict radii across `r radius_temporal_n` matched continental-group–age combinations. Negative signed contributions are truncated only for this display; missing combinations are non-estimable.
:::

::: {#suppfig-radius-change}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-37-spd-radius-change.png){width=90% fig-alt="Temporal SPD-radius changes."}

**Temporal SPD-radius changes.** The spatially controlled analysis reports 500-minus-250 km change in zero-truncated human allocation for matched continental-group–age combinations. Negative values shift toward climate; missing changes are non-estimable.
:::

::: {#suppfig-event-temporal}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-39-event-temporal.png){width=90% fig-alt="Temporal event inclusion profiles."}

**Temporal human-event profiles.** The spatially controlled analysis compares the three human-predictor definitions in `r event_temporal_n` matched continental-group–age combinations. Negative signed contributions are truncated only for display; missing combinations are non-estimable.
:::

::: {#suppfig-event-change}
![](figures/supplementary-figure-40-event-change.png){width=90% fig-alt="Temporal event inclusion changes."}

**Temporal human-event changes.** The spatially controlled analysis reports changes from SPD-only in matched continental-group–age combinations. Negative values shift the zero-truncated human allocation downward; missing changes are non-estimable, and event evidence is not independent validation.
:::
